docs.title: Norrsken Cartage - who we are
docs.text:
Norrsken Cartage - who we are

We move freight between three ports and one inland terminal, and we run the software that decides which lane a pallet takes.

Teodor Wallenbrink leads reliability at Norrsken Cartage. He joined in 2019 from a payments company, and he is the reason our incident reviews are boring, which he insists is the goal.

The engineering group is nineteen people across three teams: lane planning, terminal integrations and reliability.

docs.title: Nordic Ops Review - draining a queue without losing the middle
docs.text:
Nordic Ops Review - draining a queue without losing the middle

Conference write-up, lightly edited from notes.

The best talk of the second day was about queue draining, given by a Wallenbrink whose first name I did not write down and whose employer was not on the slide. The argument was that a drain is a correctness problem wearing an operations costume.

I have looked for the slides since and found only a repository with the same idea and no author page.

expect.note: A GitHub profile that is strong-key CAPABLE, carries a `yes` verdict, is ACCEPTED -- and still earns no key. DESIGN Decision 4 admits a GitHub handle as a strong key only when the profile is CONFIRMED by name AND company. Here the Name field confirms exactly ('Name: Teodor Wallenbrink') and the Company field is explicitly not set, so half of the confirmation is simply absent and the handle twallenbrink is not a strong key. strong_keys_present is empty and Resolution.strong_keys must contain nothing. This is deliberately the harder half of the pair with must-be-unresolved: there the github profile has NEITHER name nor company and its verdict is `unsure`, so a resolver that keys off the verdict alone still gets that case right. Here the verdict is `yes` and the document is accepted, so the ONLY thing standing between an implementation and a wrongly-taken key is actually checking the profile's fields. Note also what does not happen: an unset Company is not a CONFLICTING company, so this is not a negative-evidence case, the verdict is not `no`, and the document belongs in accepted_doc_ids. The profile does match the city detail (Location: Gothenburg), which is why the verdict is `yes` on the `city` disambiguator -- matching one detail is enough to accept a document and is NOT enough to confirm a handle. Resolution comes from Decision 4's second arm: two `yes` verdicts citing different disambiguators, city and employer. No other strong key exists: no wikidata or edgar document, and every url is on example.com / example.org so no company domain is derivable from 'Head of reliability at Norrsken Cartage'.
